verb_slots.rule: the 6-verb exp51 inventory split 3/3 into DISJOINT slots at the registered generator seed; event 1 draws from V_A, event 2 from V_B (doc 55 SS4.2). Disjointness is what makes the verb-indexed query well-posed and is what costs exp69 any claim about discourse-position resolution (doc 55 SS11).

meta.part_b_budget_note: Part A has exactly |B| x |N| = 4 x 20 = 80 casts; no draw is needed.
meta.split_unit: CAST -- a (bearer, non-bearer) pairing; never within a pair, and SHARED between the T = 1 and T = 2 item sets so doc 55 SS6.10(b)'s qualitative control compares like with like
meta.heldout_is: UNSEEN PAIRINGS, not unseen nouns (doc 55 SS4.5). Every noun's feature is in-inventory by construction, which is what makes the inventory-wide PCA fit (Part A) and the inventory-wide positional-featurizer fit (Part B, doc 55 SS18.4) legitimate, and what makes doc 55 SS11's scope limit binding: exp69 does NOT test novel-filler generalisation.

coverage_assertion.rule: every bearer AND every non-bearer in >= 1 TRAIN cast; every verb of V_A and V_B in >= 1 train item; both surface orders for EACH event slot in train; both query values in train and test in exactly equal proportion (doc 55 SS4.5)

meta.schedule_rule: verb pair by stride 5 mod 9, surface-order pair by stride 3 mod 4, unqueried-event roles by (cast + slot) mod 2, query index by a per-cast permutation of [1,1,1,2,2,2]. Strides are coprime to their moduli so no nuisance variable is confounded with the slot index, and every marginal is RE-MEASURED in the V-suite rather than assumed.
meta.question_template: الذي [v] هل هو [MARKER] -- 'the one who [v] -- is he a [CATEGORY]?'. doc 55 SS16.1's three surface questions were answered in the affirmative by the user (doc 55 SS18.1, verbatim 'yes to all three'), which is what released datagen. The SAME template is used at T = 1 and T = 2 so the SS6.10(b) control differs only in the number of events.
meta.construction: Q69 (doc 55 SS4.2): a text of T events over ONE two-referent cast with exactly one category bearer, followed by a question NAMING ONE OF THE VERBS. The label is 1 iff the agent of the NAMED event is a bearer. The twin exchanges agent and patient WITHIN the queried event only; the other event is byte-identical and the question surface is identical, so any function of the cast alone scores EXACTLY 0.500 and the classes are 50/50 by construction. Each event is rendered independently as SVO or VSO -- the alternation the archived pregroup reader implements (archive/01_parser_pipeline/arabic_dep_reader.py:130-138, 167-180).
invariants_asserted: test casts disjoint from train and val casts (unseen pairings)
the T = 1 and T = 2 item sets share ONE cast split
every bearer and every non-bearer appears in >= 1 train cast
every pair: identical cast, identical wire order, identical question spec, identical surface order flags, opposite answers
roles exchanged in the QUERIED event only; the other event is byte-identical across twins, sentence included
exactly one bearer in every cast
answer == yes iff the agent of the QUERIED event is a real bearer
the queried verb occurs in EXACTLY ONE event (V8, doc 55 SS7.5)
answer classes balanced in every split at every T
n_test == 300 at each T, matching exp60/exp61/exp68 so doc 55 SS6's 0.06 bar transfers exactly

comparator.reading_rule: If (i) the RAW comparator TIES the circuit, THE ENTANGLED MAP ADDED NOTHING EXTRACTABLE -- the two raw coordinates already carry everything the circuit got out of them, and the map is a reparameterisation however exotic its span. If (i) FAILS to tie but (ii) the FUNCTION-CLASS-MATCHED comparator TIES, THE MAP GENUINELY RESHAPED THE FUNCTION CLASS -- the information needed a nonlinear reorganisation the raw coordinates do not offer linearly, and the encoding supplied it.
comparator.clifford_consequence: the joint-state comparator for N-across is the SAME FUNCTION CLASS as EA-ctrl's -- <X(x)X> is identically zero under the CZ map and <Y(x)Y> is identically zero without it, and both sets span the same 9 dimensions. The comparator therefore CANNOT separate N-across from EA-ctrl, and that is registered as a PROPERTY OF THE DESIGN rather than discovered as a null. Any measured N-across vs EA-ctrl difference is TRAINABILITY or INDUCTIVE BIAS, NEVER CAPACITY.
comparator.why_the_outer_square: the 4-dim real amplitude vector is the smaller and more tempting feature, and it is WRONG: readouts are expectation values, QUADRATIC in amplitudes, so a linear model on amplitudes is a strictly WEAKER class than the circuit's and would MANUFACTURE A SPURIOUS CIRCUIT WIN. The outer square is the function-class-matched object. Stated because choosing the amplitudes would have been an easy and invisible error.

comparator.function_class_qualifier: doc 56 SS8.5: 'identical features' makes each comparator a RESTRICTION of the circuit's conditional function class -- the circuit carries one form PER CONDITIONING GROUP (12 at T = 1, 72 at T = 2, doc 55 SS5), the comparator carries one TOTAL. A comparator loss on a T = 2 cell is therefore even less automatically a circuit win. This qualifier travels with every number in this file.

dcc_map.note: the ANGLE-MAP interaction within the product-register family. DESCRIPTIVE CONTEXT ONLY (doc 56 SS4.3): P-eps against the old map differs in angle map, so differencing them is a population mismatch in doc 47 SS18.5's sense.

composition_cost_doc56_SS6_7.no_confident_direction_for_cc_N_in: doc 56 SS6.7, registered: the precedents GENUINELY CONFLICT. A single RY composes essentially for free (cc_A = +0.0040, cc_M = +0.0033, doc 55 SS20.3); a product register COLLAPSES under composition (cc_W = +0.2527, same source); and AN ENTANGLED REGISTER HAS NO PRECEDENT in this programme or, per doc 56 SS2, in the literature. Either branch is readable and neither is a surprise. The nearest precedent for cc_P-eps is R2-W's collapse, since P-eps is the same product-register family on a different map; that is stated as the EXPECTATION and not as a criterion.
composition_cost_doc56_SS6_7.population_note: doc 56 SS6.9(b) refuses any T = 1 vs T = 2 accuracy DELTA as a CRITERION, because R1 and R2 are different tasks with different label distributions and differencing them is doc 47 SS18.5's population mismatch. SS6.7 registers the same difference as a DESCRIPTIVE quantity, and the distinction is exactly that: reported, never read.

grade3.method_note: doc 56 SS9.3 / SS10 note 1: the N-across and EA-ctrl percentiles are computed at the METHOD-MATCHED two-stage value 0.9250 against a two-stage null, because no three-stage null exists. The verdict is robust to the choice -- 0.9625 > 0.9250 > 0.7940 -- so the category is above its null under either reading.
grade3.verdict: UNTESTABLE THIS RUN -- no exp70 arm has a below-null category (P-eps 92.5th percentile, N-in 98.0th, N-across 92.0th, EA-ctrl 92.5th). Recorded rather than quietly dropped, exactly as doc 55 SS19.2 recorded it for exp69.
grade3.structural_observation_DESCRIPTIVE: doc 56 SS9.3: N-in and P-eps both reach 1.0000 but their NULLS differ -- N-in's size-matched null mean is 0.8991 +/- 0.0572 against P-eps's 0.9429 +/- 0.0403, putting the real category at the 98.0th percentile for N-in and the 92.5th for P-eps. The 36-dimensional E-in space interpolates random labellings LESS than the 81-dimensional product space while still reaching the real category's ceiling. Reported because two identical 1.0000s are NOT identical instruments. It licenses nothing (doc 52 SS2.2).

verdicts.anchors_replicate_exp69_note: INAPPLICABLE ON A FRESH DRAW. doc 56 SS6.1's gate compares per-seed accuracies against exp69's measurements on EXP69'S OWN FROZEN ITEMS; the confirm draw has different items, so there is nothing to compare against and a 'pass' would be manufactured. The codepath it certifies was gated on the FIRST draw and PASSED BIT-EXACTLY on all four arms (bit-exact), and this run shares that code byte-for-byte. CONSEQUENCE CARRIED: doc 56 SS5.3 omitted the anchor families' floors on the argument that the |delta| <= 0.002 gate was transitively stronger than re-measuring them. THAT ARGUMENT DOES NOT SURVIVE A FRESH DRAW. The anchor arms are therefore UN-FLOORED DESCRIPTIVE BASELINES on this draw and NO BOOLEAN READS THEM; they are not silently promoted to gated arms, and two new floor families were not invented to rescue them (that would add 20 runs the registration never authorised, on the draw whose entire job is to re-test ONE registered boolean).

the_one_directional_call_doc56_SS9_4.why_it_was_registered: TRUE -- THE ONE DIRECTIONAL CALL IN THE DOC. The only cell where doc 56 SS2's query-1 barren-plateau mechanism and doc 55 SS20.3's register-collapse-under-composition finding AGREE. Registered as the falsifiable prediction of the run.
the_one_directional_call_doc56_SS9_4.reading: doc 56 SS9.4 registered exactly ONE directional call, and doc 56 SS18 item 2 recorded IN ADVANCE that it rests on an ANALOGY: the barren-plateau literature concerns visible/hidden splits in deep QNNs, not a two-qubit encoding register, and doc 55 SS20.3's collapse concerns a PRODUCT register. Two lines of evidence pointing the same way is better than one, and it is still not a precedent. It came back TRUE and doc 56 SS11 makes it the run's headline -- which MAY NOT BE CLAIMED ON THE FIRST DRAW ALONE: the confirm draw at generator seed + 1000 with all arms present is MANDATORY (doc 47 SS18).

T1_intra.comparator_clause_note: doc 56 SS6.4 requires SS8.4's comparator clause not to block, and SS8.4 is doc 55 SS8.2/SS8.3 inherited and EXTENDED TO THE COMPARATOR PAIR. Applied here in its faithful form: a POSITIVE circuit gap that clears the 0.06 bar while the comparator gap on the SHARED tier does not is an artefact of the control arm's trainability and MAY NOT be claimed. It is deliberately NOT applied to the `hurts` direction, because a negative circuit gap with no comparator gap IS the trainability reading, and SS8.4 row 2 registers that as a legitimate, reportable outcome rather than a blocked one. Blocking it would suppress exactly the branch doc 56 SS2's query-1 literature predicts.
